requirements_summary: Workloads: primary: chat support assistant and contextual doc search; secondary: nightly reranking and embeddings refresh.
Targets: p95 latency < 150ms for chat; embedding throughput >= 200 QPS during business hours; reranking jobs can be batched off-peak.
Cost sensitivity: moderate-high — tight SaaS margins, target to reduce per-embedding unit cost by >=35% vs current hosted plan.
Model preferences: open/Redwood-verified models ok; prefer ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback to cheaper variants under heavy load.
Routing/fallback: prefer smart routing by region + tiered variants (low-cost quantized variant fallback for non-critical paths).
Security: must support SSO/SAML for admin console, KMS integration for keys, audit logs retained 1 year, EU data residency for EU customers.
Operational: need per-route cost telemetry, token-level breakdown for chargeback to business units, and alerting on quality regressions after model changes.
cost_optimization_workshop_findings: Batching: continuous batching in Dedicated reduced average token CPU usage by ~28% in POC; recommended batch size 8–12 for embeddings endpoints.
Caching: prefix/KV cache on chat routes yielded 2.4x effective cost reduction for repeated prompts; suggested 30% of traffic eligible for caching.
Quantization profiles: int8 + targeted kernelization produced ~1.8x throughput improvement with minor quality delta (manual eval pass required for critical flows).
Unit economics: extrapolated ARR impact — switching to Dedicated with recommended autoscale and caching could save ~$60k–$95k annually at forecasted volume (based on current traffic profile).
Operational levers: enable model-level fallback policies for cost vs latency; use hot-path and cold-path routing to isolate expensive reranking from chat SLOs.
